title: RemoteFunction:InvokeServer()
summary: Client asks the server a question and YIELDS until answered: returns whatever the server's OnServerInvoke returns. Use sparingly — it blocks your thread for a network round trip.

parameters.name: ...args
parameters.description: Sent to the server; OnServerInvoke receives them after the automatic Player parameter.

reference.returns: Whatever the server's OnServerInvoke handler returns (serialized back). Errors if no handler is assigned; propagate handler errors to the caller.

details.heading: Yields
details.body: The calling thread pauses until the server responds. Never call in RenderStepped or other framerate-critical code.

explanation.whatItIs: A function call that happens to cross the network: ask, wait, get the answer.
explanation.whyItExists: Sometimes you truly need data back — prices, permissions, generated content — and waiting is acceptable.
whenToUse: On-demand data fetches where the client waits anyway (opening the shop menu)
whenNotToUse: Every frame, every input, or in any hot loop
When the answer doesn't need to be immediate — event-driven updates are cheaper
tips: pcall it: handlers can error or be unassigned
Server handler signature: function(player, ...args) — same player-first rule as OnServerEvent
commonMistakes: Invoking before the server assigned OnServerInvoke → error
Chaining: server invokes the invoking client back inside the handler → deadlock

examples.title: Fetch shop prices on menu open
examples.code:
-- Server:
local rf = game.ReplicatedStorage.Remotes.GetShop
rf.OnServerInvoke = function(player)
    return { Sword = 250, Potion = 50 }   -- could vary per player
end

-- Client:
local rf = game.ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("Remotes"):WaitForChild("GetShop")

local ok, prices = pcall(function()
    return rf:InvokeServer()
end)
if ok and prices then
    for item, price in prices do
        print(item, price)
    end
end
